At LDGerrits Bootstrapper 1.2.2, the proposed chain loses A: run's result contains only modules whose requested method existed and succeeded. A has no init and C's failing init is excluded; only B can reach the chained start, provided its init succeeds. Ignoring the error result also crosses the phase barrier despite C's failure.

Retain the original loaded module list for both synchronous phases. Check load errors before dispatch; run .init, inspect its error map, and prevent .start while initialization failed. Bootstrapper continues within the current run sequence, so the caller must handle partial initialization and owned rollback. Once initialization is valid, run .start against the original list, allowing A's start-only method to participate, and check start errors too. The dot prefix passes owner as context without injecting self. These behaviors are documented in the supplied [API/lifecycle reference](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/15925872650c/skill-revision-work/session-a/skills/roblox-resource-acquisition/children/roblox-bootstrapper-1-2-2/references/api-and-lifecycle.md).

Give the feature one application-level dispose function, shared by close and respawn. It should mark the feature disposed and detach retained owners before cleanup, so repeated or reentrant calls invoke each raw Janitor's Destroy at most once.

Use explicit producer and consumer phases: disconnect producers first, then destroy views. Separate Janitors or equivalent owned cleanup groups make that order explicit. Protect each top-level phase, and isolate each potentially throwing entry in a protected, nonthrowing callback so one failure cannot skip unrelated required cleanup. Establish owners before acquisition and register resources immediately, using explicit Disconnect, Destroy, or callback cleanup methods.

Janitor 1.18.3 supplies neither insertion-order cleanup nor best-effort continuation. A throwing entry can abort traversal and leave CurrentlyCleaning set; retry is not a reliable recovery strategy. Successful raw Destroy also clears its table and metatable, so repeated raw destruction is unsupported. See the supplied [Janitor lifecycle reference](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/15925872650c/skill-revision-work/session-a/skills/roblox-resource-acquisition/children/roblox-janitor-1-18-3/references/api-and-lifecycle.md).

The provider owns the borrowed LemonSignal 2.0.0 signal; this feature owns only its subscription and work. Destroying the shared signal disconnects other consumers and can leave Wait suspended. Neither Destroy nor Disconnect cancels an already-running callback. Destroy also does not permanently close the signal, so another consumer reconnecting is permitted behavior.

Replace Wait with an explicitly retained Connect subscription, using a settled/disposed guard if only one result is wanted. Disconnect that handle on delivery or disposal, cancel separately owned waiting/tasks where supported, and recheck disposal after any yield before applying results. Destroy only feature-created signals or wrappers and discard disposed feature handles.

If the old Wait task is still suspended, its owner must cancel that task; task cancellation alone does not remove Wait's hidden connection from a borrowed long-lived signal. The retained-subscription pattern avoids that ownership problem. These limits are documented in the supplied [LemonSignal lifecycle reference](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/15925872650c/skill-revision-work/session-a/skills/roblox-resource-acquisition/children/roblox-lemonsignal-2-0-0/references/api-and-lifecycle.md).

The client feature should own an idempotent teardown wrapper around its Vide mount. Inside the component's scope, register the root Frame with cleanup immediately after creation and parent owned children beneath that root; create does not automatically establish Instance cleanup ownership.

On close, mark disposal and detach the retained raw disposer before invoking it. Stop feature-owned producers first, then dispose the UI scope, protecting independent phases. Repeated close events should reach the wrapper and find no remaining raw disposer. Keep cleanup callbacks nonthrowing or individually protected: this Vide 0.4.1 commit uses insertion order, and one throwing callback can prevent later cleanup.

Remove step(0) from component teardown. It disconnects Vide's package-global stepper and can affect other components; it is a host-level finalizer, not this gameplay component's disposer. The supplied [Vide lifecycle reference](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/15925872650c/skill-revision-work/session-a/skills/roblox-resource-acquisition/children/roblox-vide-0-4-1/references/api-and-lifecycle.md) defines these exact-target limits; no runtime teardown pass is implied here.

Both reactive assumptions need correction. Charm 0.11.1 and Vide have separate tracking graphs, so a raw Charm getter in a Vide property does not establish a Vide subscription. Discarding the listener disposer loses explicit teardown ownership. Charm's default equality compares values/references, not table contents; mutating and resetting the same table normally suppresses notification. Use immutable replacement, including changed nested tables. Studio's frozen defaults can also reject mutation.

Use a minimal owned bridge inside a Vide scope, reusing a project adapter when one is supplied. Seed a Vide source from the Charm getter, then keep an owned Charm subscription updating that source; GUI properties read the Vide source. Register an enclosing cleanup callback with a retained-disposer slot before activating the subscription, then store the returned disposer immediately. Dispose that producer before its consumer disappears. If using subscribe, seed explicitly because it skips the initial callback; listen supplies an initial callback. Keep reactive callbacks synchronous and separately own any nested effects. See the supplied [Charm guidance](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/15925872650c/skill-revision-work/session-a/skills/roblox-resource-acquisition/children/roblox-charm-0-11-1/SKILL.md) and [lifecycle details](sandbox:/workspace/scratch/15925872650c/skill-revision-work/session-a/skills/roblox-resource-acquisition/children/roblox-charm-0-11-1/references/api-and-lifecycle.md).
